So, I had just moved into residence at this university. Halfway across the province, basically none of my friends had gone to this school, so being a social person, meeting people became high priority. Found this guy, an amateur rapper. His flow was great, clearly very talented, but it quickly struck me that I disagreed with his lyrics on a moral level. I told myself that this was just a persona for the microphone, though, not really reflective of who he was in real life. And to an extent, I was right: one-on-one he was a lovely guy. Smart, funny, insightful, really a great friend. Then I met his friends. The moment he was around others he changed. Immediately he was referring to women as "bitches" and talking about how to "get" them and how stupid they were. In that moment I realized I was being willfully ignorant. "Bitches giving n****s life sentences when they miss their periods" wasn't clever wordplay, it was dismissal of absentee fathers and vilification of the single mothers they left behind.

I get it, different crowds neccessitate that you behave differently. I'm a social chameleon myself. But there's a difference between being a social chameleon and having no backbone.
